categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: the Trust has taken several steps, working closely with the Matron and ward manager responsible for the ward on these issues. It is the practice on this ward to hold a daily
promises.summary: Daily multidisciplinary board rounds to improve discharge planning

concerns.quote: the Discharge procedure followed in respect of Mr. Watts' discharge from the Princess Royal Hospital in Haywards Heath, West Sussex on the 4" December 2014 was deeply flawed. There was no ongoing process of discharge.
The discharge paperwork was effectively blank.

There was no communication as to the discharge, either with regard to the anticipated date of discharge or with the Nursing Home who were expected to receive him back or with Graham Watts' son. He was medically unfit for discharge arriving back at his Nursing Home hypothermic, hypotensive, oedematous and sleepy.
It is acknowledged and accepted that a change of environment increases the risks of fall.
Evidence was heard to the effect that if Mr. Watts had not fractured his hip when he fell, he would not have died when he did.

These incorporate a range of actions relating to the workforce, education, environment, equipment, patient flow, teamwork and communications.
promises.summary: Introduced new clinical management structure to improve AMU functioning

concerns.quote: Once again my concerns involve the Acute Medical Unit (AMU).
Mrs. KENNEDY was transferred from AMU in a chair, not a trolley.
Handover was incomplete and unhelpful.
She had porridge leaking from her mouth; it took 20 mouth sponges to give her adequate mouth care.
concerns.hazard: porridge leakage and inadequate mouth care

concerns.quote: She felt cold and said she was cold.

reports.title: Patricia Webb
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: At the Inquest | was told that on Emerald Ward the Nursing staff have a higher awareness of the risk of falls because so many of their patients are at high risk. However, they provide no specialling. Presumably the rationale for this is that they are extremely good at their job and are able to take care of their patients without specialling. Demonstrably in Mrs [name redacted] case this did not happen
concerns.hazard: falls on Emerald Ward without adequate monitoring

concerns.quote: There was a plan in mid-September put in place by the Dementia Nurse for Mrs Webb to have increased levels of observation, for her to be engaged in meaningful activity and for allowing her to be mobile but using non slip footwear and a mobility aid. With regard to the observations | really could not see any evidence that this was giving her enhanced protection. When analysing the falls and their timing it was clear that they always happened early in the morning and often round about the end of the
concerns.hazard: lack of implementation of observation and activity plan

concerns.quote: Non slip footwear however, is surely much easier to provide. | know that the hospital footwear comprises 'short socklets' in different sizes (thus the right size is always difficult to obtain) with non-slip soles.
concerns.hazard: inadequate non slip footwear causing fall risk

concerns.quote: In the Royal Sussex County Hospital, | understand there is to be or already taking place a trial of 'buzzer alerts' for Nurses - | am sure this is an extremely good idea but feel that it may be more profitable to be proactive rather than reactive.

The final area which concerns me is handover. It is such an important time for exchange of information so that appropriate care can be given to each individual patient and from what | heard at Mrs [name redacted] the handover relies more and more on the notes and the notes are relying more and more on tick boxes which are simply not adequate to deal with the individualities of each patient.

During the course of this Inquest | heard that it was very difficult to obtain extra resources for some of the things which were discussed. | suggested that possibly local appeals could be useful and maybe even an article in the local newspaper engaging the local community in an important Ward given that it deals with many elderly demented patients waiting for discharge to ongoing care within the community.
concerns.hazard: lack of community engagement for resource allocation

reports.title: Joan Blaber: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Historic and ongoing failure to comply with Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations (COSHH)
Failures in training (both Trust and Agency Staff) and in particular to ensure that training has been understood and retained
concerns.hazard: inadequate training on hazardous substance handling

concerns.quote: Confusion in roles. Mixing the roles of the cleaners with those members of staff who should only be dealing with food and water
concerns.hazard: role confusion between cleaning and food handling staff

concerns.quote: Failure to communicate important practices/protocols eg. water jug system
concerns.hazard: lack of communication of safety protocols

concerns.quote: Failure in training and post training monitoring for Trust staff and lack of control over training for agency staff using hazardous substances
concerns.hazard: insufficient training monitoring and control for agency staff

reports.title: Kenneth Whittington
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Mr. [name redacted] initial operation was abandoned because on his pre operation assessment on the 23 March 2018 there was no Junior Doctor present
concerns.hazard: no junior doctor present during pre-operative assessment

concerns.quote: Most importantly post operation 'paperwork' contained no instructions regarding the management of his urinary catheter or how long it was to remain in situ
concerns.hazard: lack of post-operative catheter management instructions

concerns.quote: Immediately post operatively Mr. [name redacted] epidural became disconnected. He complained of increasing pain over the ensuing night and in spite of this nobody, not even the most senior Nurses, ever checked his epidurall
concerns.hazard: epidural disconnection unmonitored causing uncontrolled pain

concerns.quote: Mr. Whittington was due to be discharged on the 4" May. His discharge documentation which acts as a handover for his Doctors was barely completed and this lack of completion is unacceptable
